claim: Single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) enables cellular mRNAs to be imaged at single-molecule resolution through the hybridization of a set of complementary oligonucleotide probes, each labeled with a fluorescent dye.
source: Single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) enables cellular mRNAs to be imaged at single-molecule resolution through the hybridization of a set of complementary oligonucleotide probes, each labeled with a fluorescent dye.
evidence: This is a description of the smFISH technique based on established scientific knowledge and methodology.

claim: Recent improvements in smFISH permit mRNA transcripts to be visualized in the dense heterogenous tissue of intact Drosophila brains.
source: Recent improvements in smFISH permit mRNA transcripts to be visualized in the dense heterogenous tissue of intact Drosophila brains (Long et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work by Long et al., 2017 and Yang et al., 2017.

claim: Olfactory learning in Drosophila depresses cholinergic synaptic connections between odor-specific mushroom body Kenyon cells (KCs) and mushroom body output neurons (MBONs).
source: Olfactory learning in Drosophila depresses cholinergic synaptic connections between odor-specific mushroom body Kenyon cells (KCs) and mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) (Barnstedt et al., 2016; Cohn et al., 2015; Handler et al., 2019; Hige et al., 2015; Owald et al., 2015; Perisse et al., 2016; Séjourné et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Dopamine-driven plasticity is mediated by cAMP-dependent signaling and associated kinases such as calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) and protein kinase A (PKA).
source: Dopamine-driven plasticity is mediated by cAMP-dependent signaling and associated kinases such as calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) and protein kinase A (PKA) (Boto et al., 2014; Handler et al., 2019; Hige et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2007; Qin et al., 2012; Tomchik and Davis, 2009; Yu et al., 2006; Zhang and Roman, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Mammalian CaMKII mRNA is transported to neuronal dendrites, where it is locally translated in response to neuronal activity.
source: Mammalian CaMKII mRNA is transported to neuronal dendrites, where it is locally translated in response to neuronal activity (Bagni et al., 2000; Miller et al., 2002; Ouyang et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on mammalian CaMKII.

claim: Drosophila CAMKII is critical for behavioral plasticity.
source: Drosophila CAMKII is critical for behavioral plasticity (Griffith, 1997; Malik et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Drosophila CAMKII is thought to be locally translated.
source: and is also thought to be locally translated (Ashraf et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: CaMKII smFISH probes labeled 56 ± 5 discrete puncta within each calyx.
source: CaMKII smFISH probes labeled 56 ± 5 discrete puncta within each calyx (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: smFISH probes directed to the α1 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) subunit labeled 33 ± 2 puncta in the calyx.
source: In comparison, smFISH probes directed to the α1 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) subunit labeled 33 ± 2 puncta in the calyx (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: Puncta were diffraction limited and the signal intensity distribution was unimodal, indicating that they represent single mRNA molecules.
source: Puncta were diffraction limited and the signal intensity distribution was unimodal (Figure 1D–D'), indicating that they represent single mRNA molecules.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-D' and inference from the unimodal distribution.

source: This differential localization of the CaMKII and nAChRα1 mRNAs within neurons of the mushroom body is indicative of cell specificity.
evidence: This claim is an inference drawn from the differential localization data presented.

claim: YFP smFISH probes detected half the number of CaMKII mRNAs in γ5β'2a MBON dendrites compared to CaMKII-specific probes.

claim: YFP probes hybridized to YFP-negative control brains produced background signal that was statistically distinguishable in brightness from genuine smFISH puncta.
